text: The papers' own reading of the body
why: Holmes has already mentioned the press's surmise and theories about the case, and he has read the papers, so a press reading of the body is a reasonable reference even though the specific account is not given.
Paragraph 35 describes the bowl-shaped depression where the body was found; 'the hollow' is a plain paraphrase.

text: The red and black silk cravat
why: Paragraph 35 states that Straker clasped a red and black silk cravat in his left hand.
Paragraph 35 states that the overcoat was flapping from a furze-bush.
Paragraph 35 states that Straker held a small knife in his right hand.
The label asserts the knife belonged to an assailant. The story only says Straker held the knife and that the wound came from some sharp instrument, so whose blade it was is not established.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush?
why: The overcoat is found flapping on a furze-bush away from the body, so asking how it got there is a plain question the story invites.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush? — torn off in the struggle
why: Straker is said to have defended himself vigorously against his assailants, so a struggle that tore off the coat is a possibility a reader has reason to consider.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush? — Straker took it off himself
why: Straker had set out in heavy rain wearing a mackintosh, so it is a reasonable possibility that he removed the coat himself.

text: Who struck the blow that killed Straker? — unknown assailants
why: The story describes Straker defending himself against his assailants and being struck by a heavy weapon, and no assailant has been identified, so 'unknown assailants' is a fair possibility.

text: What made the blow to Straker's head?
why: The story says the head was shattered by a savage blow from some heavy weapon, so asking what made the blow is a plain question.

text: What made the cut on Straker's thigh?
why: The story says the thigh wound was a long, clean cut inflicted evidently by some very sharp instrument, so asking what made it is a plain question.

text: What made the cut on Straker's thigh? — an assailant's very sharp instrument
why: The story says the cut was made by a very sharp instrument and that Straker was attacked by assailants, so an assailant's instrument is a possibility the reader has reason to consider.
